examples.knowledge_point: Calculating Scalar Triple Products Using Its Properties
examples.worked_solution:
First, we factor out the constants and get

$$
\begin{aligned}2a\cdot (b\times 3c) & =5 \\ 2\cdot [a\cdot (b\times 3c)] & =5 \\ 2\cdot 3\cdot [a\cdot (b\times c)] & =5 \\ a\cdot (b\times c) & =\frac{5}{6}.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we swap $\mathbf{a}$ and $\mathbf{c}$ to get

$$
\begin{aligned}c\cdot (b\times a) & =-\frac{5}{6},\end{aligned}
$$

and again we swap $\mathbf{a}$ and $\mathbf{b}$ to get

$$
\begin{aligned}c\cdot (a\times b) & =\frac{5}{6}.\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.worked_solution:
Remember that the scalar triple product $a\cdot (b\times c)$ is just the determinant of the matrix whose rows are given by $a,$ $b,$ and $c.$

So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}a\cdot (b\times c) & =|\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 & 4 \\ 5 & 2 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =2\cdot |\begin{aligned}3 & 4 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}|\,-\,1\cdot |\begin{aligned}0 & 4 \\ 5 & 1\end{aligned}|\,+\,0\cdot |\begin{aligned}0 & 3 \\ 5 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =2\,(3\cdot 1-4\cdot 2)\,-\,1\,(0\cdot 1-4\cdot 5)\,+\,0\,(0\cdot 2-3\cdot 5) \\  & =2\,(-5)\,-\,1\,(-20)\,+\,0\,(-15) \\  & =-10+20+0 \\  & =10.\end{aligned}
$$
